# 🔍 Mobile App — Analysis

## The Problem

The current web-only experience forces mobile users to juggle a desktop-oriented interface on small screens, resulting in high drop-off rates during onboarding. The core data model is sound but the presentation layer was never adapted for touch. A dedicated mobile app removes this friction without requiring a full rewrite of the backend.

## Hard Constraints

- iOS and Android must ship simultaneously — a single React Native codebase is the agreed approach.
- The existing REST API (`/api/v2`) is the only backend interface; no new endpoints for v1.
- App Store review cycles impose a 2-week minimum between feature freeze and public release.
- The team has two mobile engineers and one designer; no additional headcount before launch.

## Open Questions

- **Push notifications**: Should v1 include push, or defer to v2? Options: (a) defer entirely, (b) critical alerts only (booking confirmations), (c) full notification suite.
- **Offline mode**: The braindump mentions offline reading but not offline writes. Options: (a) read-only cache, (b) optimistic writes with sync queue, (c) no offline support.
- **Auth strategy**: Native biometric (Face ID / fingerprint) vs. re-using the existing web JWT flow. Options: (a) biometric-gated JWT refresh, (b) plain email/password for v1, (c) OAuth with Apple/Google.

## Dependencies & Sequencing

- API `/api/v2` must be stable before the mobile team integrates — any breaking changes cascade to the app.
- Design system tokens must be exported to React Native before component work begins.
- App Store / Google Play developer accounts must be active before any TestFlight or internal testing.

## Explicitly Out of Scope

- **Admin dashboard**: Mentioned in the braindump but belongs in a separate web-only epic — reason: different user persona, longer horizon, no mobile use-case.
- **In-app payments**: Requires App Store compliance work that would delay launch by 4–6 weeks.
- **Real-time collaboration**: Network complexity is disproportionate to v1 value — re-scope for v2 when user base is established.

# 🎯 Epic: Mobile App

## Business Value

Mobile users represent 68% of the product's organic traffic but convert at half the rate of desktop users. A native mobile app removes the primary adoption barrier for this segment and creates a distribution channel (App Store / Play Store discoverability) that the web product cannot access.

The competitive landscape shows three direct alternatives, all of which have native apps. Without mobile parity, enterprise sales conversations consistently stall at the IT evaluation stage — procurement teams flag the web-only footprint as an integration risk.

A successful v1 launch targeting the top three user journeys (onboarding, daily check-in, report export) is the minimum viable footprint to close this gap and unlock the mobile segment of the sales pipeline.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers

- React Native app (iOS + Android) hitting the existing `/api/v2` REST API
- Three core screens: Home dashboard, Detail view, Export/share flow
- JWT authentication with biometric unlock for returning users
- Push notifications for booking confirmation (single notification type)
- App Store and Google Play submission and review

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover

- ❌ Offline write support — deferred to v2; read-only cache is in scope
- ❌ Admin features — web-only epic, different persona
- ❌ In-app purchases or subscription management — compliance overhead
- ❌ Real-time collaboration — v2 scope

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Design system + navigation skeleton** | None | — | 3 days | High |
| 2 | **Auth flow (JWT + biometric unlock)** | Task 1 | — | 2 days | High |
| 3 | **Home dashboard + Detail screens** | Task 2 | — | 4 days | High |
| 4 | **Export/share flow + push notifications** | Task 3 | Task 3 | 3 days | High |
| 5 | **App Store + Play Store submission** | Task 4 | — | 2 days | Low |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ App published on both stores with zero critical crash reports in first 7 days
- ✅ Mobile onboarding completion rate reaches desktop parity (≥ 42%) within 30 days
- ✅ P95 screen-load latency under 800ms on a 4G connection
- ✅ At least 3 enterprise accounts complete evaluation using the mobile app

# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Mobile App

## Architecture Overview

The mobile app is a thin React Native client over the existing `/api/v2` REST backend. No new backend services are required for v1. The key architectural decision is to treat the mobile app as a first-class API consumer rather than a web view wrapper — this means full native navigation, native gesture handling, and platform-specific permission flows, while sharing 100% of the business logic expressed through the existing API contract.

State is managed with Zustand (lightweight, no boilerplate) combined with React Query for server-cache synchronisation. This pairing eliminates the dual-source-of-truth problem that plagues Redux-heavy apps: React Query owns all remote state, Zustand owns all local/ephemeral state.

Biometric authentication is layered over the existing JWT flow: the refresh token is stored in the iOS Keychain / Android Keystore, and Face ID / fingerprint unlock gates the retrieval of that token. The API sees standard Bearer tokens — no server-side changes needed.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| API consumer, not API owner | Zero new backend endpoints for v1; all features must be achievable with `/api/v2` as-is |
| Platform-native UX | Use platform navigation patterns (stack on iOS, bottom tabs shared) rather than web-ported metaphors |
| Offline-read first | Cache responses in MMKV (fast synchronous storage); never show a blank screen when offline |
| Fail visibly | Network errors surface as inline banners, not modal alerts that interrupt flow |

## Component Design

### Navigation Shell
**Purpose**: Defines the top-level route structure using React Navigation. Bottom tab navigator with three roots: Home, Search, Profile. Each root has its own stack navigator.

### Auth Module
**Purpose**: Manages the full authentication lifecycle. On first launch: email/password form → JWT issued → refresh token stored in Keychain/Keystore. On return: biometric prompt → token retrieved → silent refresh if needed.

### Data Layer (React Query + MMKV)
**Purpose**: Centralises all remote data fetching and caching. MMKV provides the persistence adapter so queries survive app restarts. Stale-while-revalidate policy means users always see cached data instantly while fresh data loads in the background.

### Export/Share Module
**Purpose**: Generates a shareable PDF or deep link from the current Detail view. Uses React Native's built-in Share sheet — no third-party dependency.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| UI framework | React Native 0.74 | Existing web team has React knowledge; single codebase for iOS + Android |
| Navigation | React Navigation 6 | Industry standard; deep-link support out of the box |
| Server state | React Query (TanStack) | Handles caching, retries, background refresh; eliminates boilerplate |
| Local state | Zustand | Minimal API, no providers, no boilerplate |
| Persistence | MMKV | 10× faster than AsyncStorage; synchronous reads for auth bootstrap |
| Secure storage | Keychain (iOS) / Keystore (Android) | Platform-native; required for biometric auth |
| Push notifications | Expo Notifications | Handles both platforms; works with bare React Native |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| React Native over Flutter | Team already knows React; shared component logic with web | Flutter would give better performance but requires Dart upskilling |
| Zustand over Redux | Negligible boilerplate; sufficient for v1 local state needs | Redux DevTools are better; Redux is worth it at larger team sizes |
| Expo Notifications over FCM/APNs directly | Single API surface; handles token registration differences | Expo dependency; harder to eject later if needed |
| MMKV over AsyncStorage | Synchronous reads unblock the auth bootstrap path | Binary format (not human-readable); harder to inspect during debugging |
